Weekly rankings

Half-PPR projections if active, with realistic ranges. Tap a player for his full card.

How to read
Projection assumes the player is active (NFL availability is yes/no, so injured players show an Inactive% instead of a discount). The range bar comes from how past projections of this size actually turned out: thin line = floor to ceiling (10th to 90th percentile), thick bar = the likely middle half, tick = projection. Matchup: grade A-F ranks this week's matchups at the position; the pill is fantasy points this defense adds or removes vs an average one. TD donut: ring segments = chance of 0 / 1 / 2 / 3+ touchdowns (darker = more), center = chance of at least one. ECR is the FantasyPros expert consensus rank (faded "lw" = last week's, until Friday). A yellow edge marks a projection boosted by a teammate's absence.
Preset
Points per stat
League (sets the tiers)

Projections are stat lines, so any scoring re-scores them exactly. Blended-in expert ranks and the floor/ceiling ranges are scaled by the same ratio (an approximation). Saved on this device.

# ECR Player Projection Actual Matchup Inactive FP/G Tier Expected line Takeaway

Matchups

Win chances, not picks. When neither side is a clear favorite we call it a tossup.

How to read
Win chance is the market's: the Vegas spread turned into a probability using how often teams with that spread have actually won. In backtests the market has been a more accurate forecaster than our model, and mixing the model in never helped, so we show the better number. Before lines are posted (lookahead weeks) the model's chance is used. Our model is shown underneath as an independent second opinion with no Vegas input: the two teams' Power ranks (play-by-play efficiency, opponent-adjusted, with the current quarterback) plus their Elo ratings (built from final scores, with memory across seasons) and home field. Hover it for the inputs. In backtests this mix beat each piece alone, though the market is still more accurate. Tossup means the favorite's chance is under 59% (roughly a spread under 3 points). Historically, favorites in that range won about as often as a coin flip would, so naming one would be false precision. The shaded middle of each bar marks that zone. A 70% favorite should still lose 3 times in 10. That is an upset the forecast expected, not a mistake; the track record above shows whether chances at each level came true as often as they claimed. Who wins each battle breaks the matchup down unit by unit (our play-by-play ratings, the same ones behind the Power ranks). Every bar is a tug of war in the two teams' colors, away team always on the left and home team on the right. Whoever pushes past the middle line wins it, and the number on the winner's side is the edge in EPA per 100 plays (expected points added: how much better each play goes than an average one from the same down, distance and field position). Each offense against the other defense: its offense rating minus the defense's, with the total weighting passing and running by that offense's projected dropbacks and runs. Tap a matchup to split it. Special teams compares the two units per 100 special-teams plays, and home field is the per-play boost the home team gets. Pace has no per-play form, so it is listed as projected plays. Rank chips are league ranks from the Power tab (green top 8, red bottom 8); the chips by the team names are overall power ranks. Hover a row for both teams' ratings. Bar length is how much each edge matters this game, on one scale for every row. The model never publishes a point spread, which is left to the market.

Power rankings

Opponent-adjusted points per game vs an average team. Everything adds up: Offense = Pass O + Run O, Defense = Pass D + Run D, Net = Offense + Defense + ST.

How to read
Every number is points per game against an average opponent: each unit's per-play rating times a league-average number of those plays (about 36 dropbacks, 25 runs and 11 special-teams plays), so the columns add up and a run edge is never read as equal to a pass edge. Hover any unit for its per-play rating. Pass O includes the team's current starting quarterback. Higher is better everywhere, including defense. Rank range is the 10th-90th percentile rank when ratings are resampled within their uncertainty (200 bootstrap resamples of games): a narrow range means the data has settled, a wide one means a few more games could move the team a lot. Colored badges are league ranks (green = top 8, red = bottom 8). Schedule: points per game the opponents took away (played) or would take away (left), unit by unit: the team's actual dropbacks against each opponent's pass defense and runs against its run defense, plus the offenses its defense faced. Positive = tougher than average; 1st = hardest. Re-scored every week with current ratings. Arrows show the move since last week.
